newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ median house price NZ$159,000 in January - REINZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ median house price NZ$159,000 in January - REINZ.

text.p: The median New Zealand house price in January 1997 was NZ$159,000 against $146,000 in January 1996, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand said on Thursday.
It said housing sales remained buoyant during the month, with sales reported by real estate agents totalling 7,815.
"The figures show a further strengthening in confidence for the housing market generally," REINZ president Colin Brown said.
He said that after the traditionally slower trading period in December, it was encouraging to see the housing market starting to reflect the competitive interest rates available.
Most regions experienced an improved market, which showed increased interest from home buyers, Brown said.
The Auckland market continued to stabilise, although some commentators predicted a levelling off of home prices, coinciding with an anticipated slow down in population growth in that region.
January figures for the Auckland region showed 2,719 home sales.
The Auckland metropolitan total of 2,406 comprised 451 sales in North Shore, 440 in Waitakere, 517 in Manukau, 89 in Papakura, and 909 in Auckland city itself.
The median price for the entire Auckland region was up $28,000 from last year to $230,000.
Brown said the short term outlook for real estate sales remained positive and he expected the recent reductions in mortgage rates to be sustained for at least the first half of the year.

He said there was still strong competition among lending institutions for housing mortgage business. The median purchase price of a home in most regions had increased, with the median price approximately $10,000 higher compared to the same month last year.
In Wellington, where an additional 167 homes had been sold compared to January 1996, the median price was $145,000, up from $138,000.
The Canterbury/Westland region experienced the greatest increase in sales for the South Island at a median price of $135,000, up from $127,000 in January 1996.
Brown said the figures confirm a return of confidence to the real estate marketplace and bode well for some stability in house sales over the next few months.
Sales for sections were also steady, with a total of 663 sections sold in January. The median price for these across the country was $65,000.
